Posted October 15, 2007

Analysis by Richard Cowan

 

All political thinking for years past has been vitiated in the same way. People can foresee the future only when it coincides with their own wishes, and the most grossly obvious facts can be ignored when they are unwelcome. George Orwell

 

I always enjoy NORML conferences because I get to see old friends, and last weekend was no exception. However, at a more substantive level there were two exceptionally rewarding presentations.

 

The first was by Russ Belville AKA Radical Russ, who was recently the winner of the Search for the Next Great Progressive Talk Radio Star sponsored by the Center for American Progress and the Jones Radio Network.

 

Belville's recent experience confirmed my views on the cowardice of the Leftwing anti-war blogosphere in dodging the drug war. I have always considered myself on the Right, for reasons that are off-topic for MarijuanaNews.com.

See

HOW THE NARCS CREATED CRACK by Richard C. Cowan

From National Review Magazine, December 5, 1986

So it was easy for me to rag on the supposed Progressives who ignore the drug war which has done far more damage to our civil liberties than the so-called war on terror.

See

Sicko and The Return of MarijuanaNews.com. The Failure of the Left to Address the Drug War. By Richard Cowan.

Russ was very candid in recounting the warnings about how criticizing the drug war was just too controversial, the third rail and too fringe even for Progressive talk radio, if one wants to be taken seriously.

 

Interestingly, Glen Grenwald, Salon's excellent anti-war blogger denounces Washington mainstream liberals for their failure to oppose Bush's zeal for wiretapping for similar reasons.

 

In the Beltway culture, granting more power to the Government -- particularly when that power is justified by The Terrorists -- is always a Serious, Inherently Good measure, because that power will be exercised by the Good, Serious Adults Who are Trusted

 

(O)ne is Serious and Responsible and Centrist/Right only if one is too sophisticated and tough to actually think that such effete and abstract things matter.

See

Now I have to admit that I have often been too optimistic about our own progress, but to paraphrase someone, everyone is entitled to his own optimism, but not his own facts.

 

This brings me to the other presentation that I found most valuable by Appalachian StateUniversity Associate Professor of Criminal Justice, Matthew Robinson. He is the co-author of the book, Lies, Damned Lies, and Drug War Statistics: A Critical Analysis of Claims Made by the Office of National Drug Control Policy.

 

Robinsons lecture included numerous graphs that used the ONDCP's own data to show how they have consistently manipulated the statistics to get more funding for doing what they claimed was successful.

 

As one reviewer describes it, they do this by critically examining six years (2000-2006) of the National Drug Control Strategy. They read through each and every annual report, looking especially for both accurate and inaccurate use of statistics and evidence of honesty and dishonesty in each report. They examined each and every claim made by ONDCP and evaluated ONDCP's stated goals (e.g., reducing drug use and drug availability).

 

What they found for each year, almost without exception, was an almost total misuse of some very simple statistics (e.g., from various annual drug surveys, such as NHSDA, ADAM, MTF). They discovered that in many instances ONDCP employed the "optimal starting and stopping points." For instance, Robinson and Scherlen found that for the 2000 strategy report ONDCP uses a baseline of 1985 that shows a decline in drug use from that year to 1999. Yet the ONDCP was not started until 1988 and the largest drop in drug use was between 1985 and 1988, with the rate remaining steady for the rest of the decade. Other reports use 1979 as a starting point (the peak of drug use).

 

On another occasion the ONDCP claims to prove that George Bush's goal during his 2002 "State of the Union speech of a 10% reduction of drug use by youth within two years was met, but uses a time period that started one year prior to Bush's speech!

 

The authors also found numerous instances where they cite declines in youth drug use during a certain period, but ignore the fact that drug use was increasing among adults

 

This will not be news to longtime readers of MarijuanaNews.com

See

Again the Media Parrots the Partnerships Prohibitionist Propaganda Even Though Reported "Changes" Are Within the Margin of Error. Emphasis in Propaganda as in Seizures Shows Drug War Really About Marijuana

But their analysis is much more complete.

 

Of course, the Drug Czar's prohibitionist propaganda is aimed at the lazy media and the true-believer prohibitionist to whom it is considered pro-drug, anti-child and Double-Plus-Ungood to question anything that the Drug Czar might say.

See 

Incestuous Amplification. Prohibitionists Do It With Their Jackboots On, But It Is Not As Much Fun As It Sounds. Analysis by Richard Cowan

Hearing Prof. Robinson was timely because I have recently found a number of drug war triumphalists declaring that victory is at hand.

 

One of the most bizarre was Victory Over Drugs, an editorial in INVESTOR'S BUSINESS DAILY on October 3rd  which was posted at 4:20 PM. Yeah.

 

They say that recent increases in the price of cocaine show an emerging victory over the illegal drug trade. When will the naysayers admit this?

 

They then go on to blame groups funded by George Soros for hiding the good news from the American people:

 

But hard evidence of victory isn't good enough for the network of nongovernmental organizations, or NGOs, that manipulate the press and even now downplay any good news on drugs

 

Not surprisingly, many of these groups are funded by left-wing billionaire and Democratic Party influence George Soros, who's made no secret of his opposition to the drug war. They form an unofficial network of NGOs that shape the news.

 

Yeah, sure.

See
More Arresting Developments. Record Marijuana Arrests Go Unreported. No Medicine Is Smoke So DEA Busts Edibles Maker.
and
Supreme Court Decision On Medical Cannabis Expected This Week. Prohibitionist Propaganda Organization Makes Itself Available for Comment Will The Media Check Their Track Record? Here It Is.

 They then support their conclusion with a graph which says that the price of cocaine on the U.S. market has jumped 24%.

 

First, remember that this is a paper for investors, so they should know about statistics.

 

Their graph shows that the price of cocaine was over $100 per gram in the 3rd quarter of 2005, but they use the 1st quarter of this year as a base, because it shows a greater increase.

 

This is precisely the sort of prohibitionist dishonesty that Prof. Robinson illustrated in his book, but the idea that a jump in just one quarter for just one drug in just one country constitutes hard evidence of victory is hardly evidence of critical thinking skills.

 

Of course, the Mexican government intervened in the violent turf wars between the various cartels and there has indeed been some sort of supply disruption in the flow of cocaine from Mexico to the US.

 

Some really nasty Mexican gangsters have been arrested and sent to the US, but the killing of Pablo Escobar in 1993 did not stop the flow of coke from Colombia, so it seems likely that supply will soon rise with the price. Or do these conservatives think that the laws of supply and demand no longer work?

See
Lou Dobbs and the Second Mexican War. Has It Already Begun? Counting the Costs of the Drugwar.

Moreover, the meth traffic from Mexico may well be more profitable, and it seems that Europe may be biding up the price of coke. The recent report that Blackwater would be fighting the drug war in the Sahara suggests that the cocaine traffic has moved across the Atlantic.

The other victory cry comes from the Weekly Standard, which has so regularly reported on our triumphs in Iraq.The Bitterest Pill, Europe Becomes Less Drug-Friendly by Jonathan V. Last shows the prohibitionist aversion to facts.

 

In light of the Investor's Business Daily claim that George Soros-funded groups form an unofficial network that shape the news it is interesting to note Last's bio:

 

Jonathan V. Last is the online editor at The Weekly Standard. He has written for the Wall Street Journal,

See

the Los Angeles Times,

the Washington Post,

See
The Myth That The Washington Post and John Walters Are Harmless; Drug Czar Puts Hyperlying About Cannabis At The Center of the War on Freedom.

the New York Post, Salon, Slate, the Washington Times, the New York Press, and other publications. Mr. Last has appeared on CNN, Sky News, and the Fox News Channel. He lives in Alexandria, Virginia.

 

Ah, yes, all controlled by Soros?

 

In any case, one would think that the online editor would also be aware of the Internets value in fact checking.

See
International Prohibition Situation Report DEAland Media Ignore News Showing Cannabis Prohibition Is Counterproductive. Coffee Shop System Survives. 

First, the idea that Europe has somehow been uniformly drug-friendly is absurd. France and Sweden are very prohibitionist, while Germany and Spain, which Last does not mention, are much more liberal.

See

The Chaos of Cannabis Prohibition In France, DEAland and Latin America. More Proof That It Is A Counterproductive Fraud.
and

Prohibition and The Prison State. Protecting Youth and Minorities. In DEAland, The UK and France Prisons Are Full.

and

But here are just a few of his worst errors.

 

Prohibitionist propaganda: The Dutch have long favored "harm reduction" rather than law enforcement in their drug-related public policies, and many coffee shops have been able to flout what rules there are regarding the sale of cannabis.

 

Fact: Coffee shops are very easy to close when they break any of the rules, and hundreds have already been closed.

From Radio Netherlands, see
Turn a blind eye or make it legal? The Dutch soft drugs dilemma by Rutger van Santen

 

Prohibitionist propaganda: Last Friday, the Dutch government banned the sale and cultivation of magic mushrooms after a series of high-profile incidents. A justice ministry spokesman promised that the law would be enforced, and coffee shops caught selling them closed down.

 

Fact: Yes, the sale of psilocybin mushrooms has been banned, but they were sold in smart shops not coffee shops.

 

Prohibitionist propaganda, Errors of omission: Last's most egregious error of omission lies in his failure to report that the Dutch rate of cannabis use (6.1%) is roughly the European average and well below that of France (8.6%), and almost exactly half of the US rate (12.2%)

See
http://www.unodc.org/pdf/research/wdr07/WDR_2007_3.5.1_annual_prevalence.pdf

 

One might think that this fact might be of interest to American readers.

 

Of course, Last is most pleased with the recurrence of reefer madness in the UK, but he has a poor grasp of the history.

 

Prohibitionist propaganda: (M)arijuana was downgraded from a Class B to a Class C drug, essentially making possession of the substance permissible for adults.

 

Fact: No, it simply gave the police the option of not arresting adults with small quantities.

See
Beyond Bonkers: UK "Reclassification" Of Cannabis Caps Weeks of Absurdity. Prime Minister Has A Drug Problem?

Prohibitionist propaganda: Robin Murray, of London's Institute of Psychiatry, explained to the Independent that a quarter of the population was particularly at risk for psychosis caused by the elevated levels of dopamine that come from cannabis use.

See
Classic Reefer Madness At London Times: "Woman who killed father 'driven mad by cannabis.'" Quacks and Hacks and Schizophrenia. Is It Paranoid to Distrust Politicized Science?

Fact: There has not been an increase in schizophrenia over the last few decades as cannabis use increased.

 

Prohibitionist propaganda: As Antonio Maria Costa, executive director of the U.N.'s Office on Drugs and Crime, summarizes it: "The harmful characteristics of cannabis are no longer that different from those of other plant-based drugs such as cocaine and heroin."

Regarding Costa, see

UN Nark's Speech To Swedish Prohibitionists May Cause Permanent Brain Damage. Illogic, Ignorance and Lying, Especially About the Dutch, Of Course.

and more on the UN that should be of interest to an online editor:
Today Is "International Anti-Drug Day" Really. And Top UN Nark Wants To Censor Internet. Anti-Prohibitionism Equated With Genocide. The Internet Community Needs To Wake Up!

Regarding Costa,

Fact: The online editor of the Weekly Standard is telling kids that the dangers of heroin and cocaine are no different from those of cannabis. That is totally irresponsible. Can he cite any other instances in which he would accept the word of a UN bureaucrat as definitive? I doubt it!

 

Prohibitionist propaganda: In Britain, it has also become apparent that the semi-legalization for adults led to a spike in usage for minors. One precinct commander in East London said that the reclassification of the drug caused "extensive and expansive" increases in use by teenagers (for whom possession was still illegal).

See
Bonkers in Britain: New Cannabis Rules Please No One, Confuse Everyone. Watching the Political Establishment Make Fools of Themselves. Analysis by Richard Cowan

Fact: There is no hard data to support that claim. Britain already had one of the highest rates of teen cannabis use in the world, so it would be absurd to argue that even full legalization for adults could increase use significantly.

 

Prohibitionist propaganda: As Neil McKeganey of GlasgowUniversity's Centre for Drug Misuse Research explained, "Society has seriously underestimated how dangerous cannabis really is."

 

Fact: The UK has been saturated with prohibitionist propaganda for years. McKeganey is simply not credible.

See
Program Notes for the MarijuanaNews World Report May 2, 2005 Drug Czar Imports Scottish Expert Who Says Cannabis As Big A Threat As Heroin. Scotland A Mess. Interview With Steve Kubby About His Case

Prohibitionist propaganda: A July 2007 study in the Lancet reported that the use of cannabis leads to an increase in psychotic outcomes, including what researchers refer to as a "dose-response" effect--meaning that the more pot you smoke, the more at risk you are.

 

Fact: The risks in most substances is dose related. The Lancet also published a ranking of the risks posed by various substances, showing that cannabis ranks well below alcohol and tobacco.

  

One could go on, but it is clear that Mr. Last is a strong supporter of state violence against cannabis users, because he thinks that it is the conservative way. It is not. Nor is Europe, even the UK, likely to follow the failed US model. If Mr. Last did a little research and fact checking, he would know better.
